- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots next period — cap forecast at +3–5% above prior peak.
- If sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model underreacts — increase forecast by 2–4% to match sentiment momentum.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon — add 1–2% to forecast for first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model overestimates mean — apply mean reversion bias: subtract 1–3% from forecast if recent 7-day average is higher than 30-day average.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 5+ days, model tends to ignore it — reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days to reflect sentiment drag.
